newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish power plant plans $1 bln new plant. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT, 21/03/97]
newsitem.headline: Polish power plant plans $1 bln new plant. [CORRECTED 11:40 GMT, 21/03/97]

text.p: (Corrects by changing lignite mine into power plant in the headline and throughout).
Poland's large power plant, the state-owned Belchatow plans to build a new $1 billion 800 megawatt lignite power plant called Belchatow 2, the company's president said on Friday.
He said that of the $1 billion $200 million would come from the new plant's share capital while $800 million would be raised from credit, a bond or eurobond issue.
"The investment in Belchatow 2 will take around $1 billion," Edward Najgebauer told a news conference.
He said Belchatow itself was ready to put up $100 million for the new plant's capital, while the remaining $100 million would come from interested investors.
Industry officials expect the investment would be virtually risk-free as demand for energy in Poland is likely to grow rapidly in the comming years.
"This is a no-risk investment, so I expect no difficulties with raising capital...the easiest would be bank credit, but we also consider a bond or a eurobond issue," Najgebauer said.
He added Belchatow was currently sending out offers of participation in the venture to interested invetors. The new power plant is to start producing energy around the year 2003.
Analysts forecast Poland's total demand for energy would rise to 230,000 gigawats by the year 2020 from 140,000 in 1997.
"Polish demand for energy will rise despite an increase in energy effectiveness of production processes," Ryszard Frydrychowski, a deputy head of Polish Power Grid Company, also present, said.
